query: For automotive exhaust catalysts, what single intervention could improve catalytic activity and durability while reducing platinum-group-metal consumption? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Atomic layer deposition of platinum group metals on high-surface-area supports can improve catalytic activity and durability while reducing platinum-group-metal consumption.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts with platinum group metals deposited on supports
generation.intervention: Atomic layer deposition of platinum group metals
generation.conditions: High-temperature exhaust gas environment, presence of reducing and oxidizing agents
generation.mechanism: Increased dispersion and utilization of platinum group metals, enhanced thermal stability
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% improvement in catalytic activity, 30% reduction in platinum-group-metal consumption, and 25% increase in durability
generation.baseline: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts without atomic layer deposition
generation.uncertainty: Dependence on specific support material, platinum-group-metal composition, and atomic layer deposition parameters

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of catalytic activity, durability, and platinum-group-metal consumption between conventional and atomic layer deposition-based catalysts
measurements: Catalytic activity (e.g., CO conversion), durability (e.g., thermal stability), platinum-group-metal consumption
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the atomic layer deposition-based catalysts show no significant improvement in catalytic activity, durability, or platinum-group-metal consumption compared to conventional catalysts, the hypothesis is falsified.
